chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whom the month of Ramadan caught while he was ill, and he died before he recovered. He said: There is no obligation upon him, but the one who recovers then dies before fulfilling the obligation must have it fulfilled on his behalf.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who dies in Ramadan while still ill and unable to fast?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the obligation to make up Ramadan fasts (*qada*) is personal and does not transfer to heirs if the individual dies before fulfilling it. This distinguishes the debt of fasting from other financial debts, emphasizing that the missed days remain the responsibility of the one who was capable of fasting but died prematurely, provided they had recovered at some point during the illness.
